records.title: Seven Gitea API routes under `/api/v1/users/{username}` (followers, following, following/{target}, starred, subscriptions, keys and gpg_keys) were registered without the `individua
Deleting a label compared the ID of the repository in the request against the organization ID of organization labels, and the two ID sequences overlap.
Adding attachments to a release checked the repository and release of an attachment but not whether it was already linked to an issue or comment.
The visibility check of Gitea user profiles was applied to GET requests only, while `POST /{username}` (follow and unfollow) required only a signed-in user.
Creating a draft release through the API returned an `assets` list that was built from a release without an ID, which matched every attachment that was not linked to a release.
`GET /api/v1/user/subscriptions` returned the metadata of every repository a user was watching without checking that the user still had access to it.
Gitea resolved the principals of an SSH certificate by searching the content of all stored public keys instead of only principal keys.
The Gitea web handlers for adding and removing reactions on issues and comments did not refuse locked issues for users without write access, although the API did.
`POST /{owner}/{repo}/topics` was registered without the sign-in middleware that provides the cross-origin protection, so a request issued by a third-party site was not rejected.
The Gitea Actions artifact v4 (Twirp) handlers read the whole request body into memory without a size limit.
Requesting `/{username}/-/repositories` for an individual user instead of an organization made the organization home handler dereference a nil organization and panic.
The Gitea OpenID association callback in the security settings accepted a positive OpenID 2.0 assertion without checking that the signed-in user had started the linking.
